table.html:
名称分子式CAS 号纯度储存条件（长）
无水乙醇C₂H₅OH64-17-5分析纯，≥99.7%密封储存于阴凉、通风的易燃液体柜中，远离火源、热源及强氧化剂，库温不宜超过30 ℃；避免阳光直射，开启后及时盖紧瓶盖，操作现场应配备干粉灭火器。
硫酸H₂SO₄7664-93-9优级纯，95%–98%置于阴凉通风的耐酸专用柜内，与碱类、金属粉末、还原剂及有机物料分区存放；保持容器严密，防止吸潮稀释和蒸气外逸，地面应做防腐蚀处理并备有应急冲洗装置。
氢氧化钠NaOH1310-73-2分析纯，≥96.0%密封存放于干燥、阴凉处，严防吸潮，并与酸类、铝及铵盐等隔离；容器口部保持清洁，避免吸收空气中二氧化碳导致表面碳酸化，不宜长期敞口或使用金属容器盛装。
丙酮C₃H₆O67-64-1色谱纯，≥99.9%储存于符合防爆要求的易燃液体仓库或专柜，温度宜控制在5–25 ℃，远离明火、火花、静电及强氧化剂；保持容器密闭和良好通风，分装时使用防静电工具并做好接地。
乙二胺四乙酸二钠C₁₀H₁₄N₂Na₂O₈·2H₂O6381-92-6分析纯，≥99.0%密封置于阴凉、干燥、避光处，防潮防晒，与强氧化剂分开存放；开封后应尽量减少暴露时间，避免吸湿结块，并按有效期先进先出管理。
硝酸银AgNO₃7761-88-8分析纯，≥99.8%避光、密封保存于棕色玻璃瓶中，置于阴凉干燥的毒害品柜内，远离有机物、还原性物质及光源；防止受热或见光分解，称量后立即密闭，废液及包装物集中回收处理。
盐酸HCl7647-01-0分析纯，36%–38%存放于通风良好的耐酸柜中，与碱类、金属粉末及氧化剂隔离，环境温度不宜超过30 ℃；保持容器密闭以防止氯化氢逸出，操作区应设置洗眼器和紧急喷淋装置。

d1.purpose: 供读者查找常用化学试剂，核对其身份、纯度和储存要求。
tasks: 按名称查找试剂，再横向核对分子式和 CAS 号。
比较试剂的纯度等级与数值范围。
逐条阅读某种试剂的储存条件，查找温度、隔离、防护和应急要求。
relations: 每一行的名称、分子式和 CAS 号共同标识同一种试剂。
纯度和储存条件属于该行试剂；储存条件中的各项要求需要结合阅读。
roles: 表头标识五种字段；每个数据行是一条独立的试剂记录。
名称是主要查找入口，分子式和 CAS 号用于身份核验。
纯度是短属性，储存条件是需要连续阅读的长文本。
keep_whole: 尽可能保持化学名称、分子式和 CAS 号完整，尤其避免拆开分子式及其下标。
尽可能保持纯度数值、百分号、比较符和数值范围完整。
尽可能保持温度数值、单位及其他有意义的短语完整。
may_wrap: 储存条件可在中文标点或自然语义边界处换行。
纯度等级与数值可在逗号处换行；较长名称可在必要时换行。
适配视口的方案空间不足，部分标识符或数值可能被迫拆分。
same_scale: 名称、CAS 号和纯度都是短字段，宽度应与各自内容相称。
分子式需为最长公式留出更多空间；储存条件应明显宽于短字段，以支持连续阅读。
d1.h_vs_v: 适配手机宽度可同时看到所有字段，但长储存说明会显著增高行，并可能拆开标识符；横向滚动可保全标识符并改善说明的阅读节奏，代价是读者需要横向移动以关联名称和储存条件。

d2.purpose: 供读者识别常用化学试剂，并查阅其规格和储存要求。
tasks: 按名称、分子式或 CAS 号定位试剂。
核对纯度，并阅读储存、隔离和操作要求。
比较不同试剂的储存条件。
relations: 每行的名称、分子式、CAS 号和纯度共同标识一项试剂及其规格。
储存条件从属于同一行的试剂，包含需要连续阅读的安全信息。
roles: 表头标识五类信息；各数据行是并列的试剂记录。
名称是主要定位入口，分子式和 CAS 号用于精确核对，纯度描述规格，末列提供较长的操作说明。
keep_whole: 尽量保持分子式、CAS 号、百分比及温度范围完整。
试剂名称和纯度等级应尽量保持可识别；窄屏内完整显示所有标识符无法兼顾。
may_wrap: 储存条件可在中文词组和标点附近自然换行，但应避免拆开数字、单位和化学名称。
较长的试剂名称和纯度说明可在语义边界换行。
same_scale: 名称、CAS 号和纯度是较短的检索或核对字段，宽度应与各自内容相称。
分子式需要容纳最长公式；储存条件承担连续阅读，通常需要明显更宽的空间。
d2.h_vs_v: 视口内容纳五列会迫使标识符和说明频繁换行，行高显著增加；允许横向滚动可保持标识符完整，并为储存说明提供更自然的行长，但读者需要横向移动来关联字段。

analysis.strengths: The first viewport shows names, complete formulas and complete CAS numbers together. Storage instructions are relatively easy to read, headers stay on one line, and the full table has only two measured word breaks.
analysis.faults: The longest name wraps, including within the chemical name. Purity and storage are entirely beyond the initial viewport, and the table requires substantial horizontal scrolling. The long storage column also produces large empty areas in the shorter fields.
analysis.spatial_logic: It gives the formula and CAS columns enough width for their longest entries, keeps names compact, and assigns most remaining space to storage prose.

analysis.strengths: Like P, it presents the three identification columns completely at first sight, keeps headers on one line, and limits measured word breaks to two. Its wider purity column provides a little more breathing room.
analysis.faults: The extra purity width does not change the visible line pattern or row heights relative to P. The longest name still wraps, and purity and storage require scrolling.
analysis.spatial_logic: It follows P's identification-first arrangement but adds 9 px to purity, increasing total scroll distance without an evident improvement in the render.

analysis.strengths: Names, formulas and CAS numbers remain visible together initially. Its narrower storage column makes the table somewhat shorter horizontally, and the even row heights create a regular grid.

rounds.insights: The scrolling layouts preserve chemical identifiers far better than the fitted layouts. In a 360 px fitted grid there is no allocation that can keep the 135 px formula, 78 px CAS entry and long storage prose comfortably whole after padding; the fitted design must choose which reading task to protect. Proposed widths are hypotheses and need rendered verification, especially for line breaks and the exact viewport boundary.

synthesis.rationale: P keeps formulas and CAS numbers whole, presents storage instructions in two or three lines, and shows the three identification columns together in the initial viewport. general: Protect chemical formulas, identifiers, values and units from disruptive line breaks when allocating width.
Judge the initial viewport as well as the complete scrolling table, especially for lookup tasks.
Allocate width according to content and reading function rather than enforcing equal columns.
specific: A 156px formula column accommodates the longest formula, and a 99px CAS column accommodates the listed identifiers.
P's 520px storage column preserves a compact three-line maximum while leaving the identification columns visible together initially.
No fitting candidate preserves all formulas and identifiers intact at this font size and padding.

U displays all five columns at once but sacrifices continuity and efficient row comparison; its finalist status is relative to the fitting class, not an endorsement as equally readable.
synthesis.uncertain: The measured word-break counts do not identify every affected semantic unit, so their practical severity requires inspection of each break. Acceptance of U depends on whether a no-scroll requirement outweighs the fragmented chemical notation and storage instructions.

ref_auto.why: The formula column is intact, but names become nearly vertical, CAS numbers break, and storage text runs to 26 lines. The table still requires horizontal scrolling despite its extreme height.

ref_equal.why: Like C, the evenly narrow columns fracture identifiers and purity values, while storage text stretches each row over a large vertical distance. Fitting the viewport does little to make the information easy to use.

d2r2A.why: Names and formulae stay whole and the rows have a steady rhythm. The initial viewport cuts through CAS numbers, however, and the narrower storage column introduces more awkward breaks than A or B.

d1r4C.why: The wider storage column is a meaningful improvement over C and E, but its paragraphs still form tall narrow blocks. Names, formulae and CAS numbers break across lines, impairing identification and comparison.

vc_pref.why: The first viewport shows complete identifying columns and the table needs less horizontal travel than A or B. Storage text is noticeably more fragmented, purity ranges split, and taller rows leave large blank areas in the identifying columns.

ref_equal.why: The table fits, but formulas, CAS numbers and purity values break across lines. The storage text forms an extremely narrow, 26-line column, producing very tall rows and large empty areas.

d2r2A.why: Names and identifiers remain whole, and the storage text reads in manageable lines. The initial viewport cuts through the CAS column, while purity and storage require substantial horizontal scrolling.

d1r4A.why: The initial viewport shows names, formulas and complete CAS numbers; purity ranges stay whole and storage text is readable. The long chemical name wraps, and the wide table requires considerable scrolling to reach storage.

d3r3A.why: Like C, it puts the three identification columns in the initial viewport and keeps purity ranges together. The long name wraps, and the extra purity width adds a little scrolling without an apparent reading benefit.

ref_auto.why: The name column reduces names almost to vertical text, CAS numbers wrap, and storage instructions form extremely long, narrow blocks. The formula column is disproportionately wide, yet scrolling is still needed to reach the last column.

ref_equal.why: Equal columns leave storage instructions in very tall, narrow blocks and split formulas, CAS numbers and purity values. The resulting row heights make comparison and lookup arduous.

d1r4A.why: Names, formulas and CAS numbers are easy to scan, and storage instructions generally fit in three lines. The initial viewport shows those first three fields together, though reaching purity and storage requires substantial scrolling and loses the name column from view.
